Command: Speak Truth; Let No Corrupt Talk Come Out
Summary: Paul's speech command: put away lying and speak truth to your neighbour, and let no corrupt communication proceed from your mouth, but only what is good for edifying.
Commandment: Putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another. Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying.
Application: Truth-telling is grounded in membership: we are members of one another, so a lie wounds the body. Edifying speech is the positive half — words that build up and minister grace to hearers.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'for we are members one of another' (Ephesians 4:25).
Function: We are members of one another, so a lie wounds the body. This comes from the apostles, not from Sinai, so the old threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was speech that builds up: put away lying, speak truth to your neighbour, and let no corrupt communication proceed from your mouth. The evil it addressed was lying and rotten talk — words that tear down instead of edifying. It restrained that evil by making edifying speech the rule: only what is good for edifying, that it may minister grace to the hearers.
